Martin Plaut, 'Eritrea: drought, hunger and malnutrition - the evidence', 27 October 2016 (metadata index 14), publishing material smuggled out by Arbi Harnet (Freedom Friday) activists, states: 'People have been forced to draw water from pits dug into the Mereb river. This row's 22 is scoped by its own source to Ethiopian refugees: the headline is 'Eritrea Quarantines Gash Barka Region, 22 Cholera cases found among Ethiopian refugees' and the Madote mirror leads with the bullet '- 22 Cholera cases found among Ethiopian refugees'. Plaut's 1342 is scoped to the resident population of Upper Gash drawing water from Mereb riverbed pits, counted at ONE makeshift clinic ('in one makeshift clinic alone'), i.e. explicitly a partial count. Different populations, different denominators, one month apart.

(b) The remainder of that article is a conspiracy piece alleging the TPLF deliberately spread Vibrio cholerae, and it carries a second uncorroborated figure ('In the Amhara regional capital city of Bahir Dar ... more than 1200 cholera cases and 60 cholera related deaths are reported'). (c) geeskaafrika.com and madote.com carry it byline-identically ('By CDE'), so it is one origin, not two.

PROVENANCE MAP OF THE WHOLE 2016 EVENT, established by reading full texts. ORIGIN A = Arbi Harnet / Freedom Friday, which is the sole origin of asmarino 4778 (10 Sep), asmarino 4794 (25 Sep), asmarino 4822 and the Plaut post (both 27 Oct), and of the sitata.com travel alert, whose reference list is the single URL asmarino 4778. ORIGIN B = byline CDE -> geeskaafrika + madote, this row. ORIGIN C = Assenna 30 Sep (metadata index 21), unattributed, whose content - Dembelas and Qwohayn as origin areas, the Agordat cordon outpost on the Keren road, halted weekly markets - appears in no Arbi Harnet dispatch and so is plausibly independent. WHY THE OUTBREAK WAS ALMOST CERTAINLY MUCH LARGER THAN 22, on evidence that does not depend on any single number. All three origins independently describe a zoba-scale cordon sanitaire: Origin B 'imposes public transports ban to and from Gash Barka region'; Origin C 'All movements into and from the area have been barred, Aqurdet being the outpost of the limited zone, coming from Keren; The weekly market days have been halted'; Origin A 'Roads have been closed, transport halted and movement into and out of the effected areas has been tightly controlled. Members of the local militia, the police and the army are closely restricting movement', plus 'the government responded ... by sending teams of doctors and local nurses to the areas hit by the epidemic' and 'Samples from patients have to be sent to the national laboratory in Asmara, to be cultured and identified.' A transport cordon with market closures, militia enforcement, deployed medical teams and a national-laboratory culture workflow is not a 22-case response, and a pro-government outlet conceding a quarantine is an admission against interest.

CROSS-BORDER PRIOR (metadata index 39). Mengistu et al., Clin Infect Dis 2024;79(Suppl 1):S8, Tables 3-4, from Ethiopian EPHI surveillance: TIGRAY region 2016 = 3328 cases, 42 deaths, incidence 64.61/100000, CFR 1.26%, within an Ethiopian national 2016 total of 29871 cases. Tigray's 1.26% CFR and Origin A's clinic CFR of 13/1342 = 0.97% are the same epidemiological regime.

On 21/09/06 a team started to investigate the out break and the physicians there suspected Cholera based clinical case definition and isolated the cases and treated them with IV fluids and antibiotics as indicated. Stool samples were taken to Asmara Central Laboratory and the results were positive for Vibrio cholerae. The outbreak was linked to drinking water from broken pipe. The investigation also revealed that all the primary cases were from Tigtig village. The few cases from Tessenei town, Fesko, Alebu and Goluj were linked to the other cases in Tessenei hospital and could have been infected in the hospital. The out break started in week 37 of September peaked in week 38 and was controlled at week 44 (Figure 4). There were a total of 60 cases and 3 deaths' - interpreted as 60 sCh cases, 3 deaths. FIRST LABORATORY-CONFIRMED ERITREAN CHOLERA OUTBREAK EVER LOCATED BY THIS PROJECT, AND THE FIRST ERITREAN SUB-ZOBA (ADM2) CHOLERA ROW. Interpreted as 60 sCh and 3 deaths; cCh left EMPTY because the source confirms V. cholerae by culture at Asmara Central Laboratory but never states how many of the 60 were culture-confirmed. CFR 5.0%, at the upper end of the plausible band and consistent with a rural outbreak reaching a district hospital late. GEOGRAPHY, and why the row sits at sub-zoba depth: the source names the administrative chain explicitly - Tigtig village -> Tessenei sub Zoba -> Gash Barka Zoba - and titles both the section and Figure 4 'Cholera Outbreak in Tessenei'. All primary cases were Tigtig village residents; the minority of cases resident in Tessenei town, Fesko, Alebu and Goluj are stated to have been infected AT TESSENEI HOSPITAL, so place of transmission for the whole 60 is Tessenei sub-zoba even though a few patients lived elsewhere in Gash-Barka. Every named locality is inside Gash-Barka, so the zoba attribution is certain and only the sub-zoba split of a handful of cases is uncertain. DATES: TL is the source's own stated onset, 18/09/06.
